Survival Japanese: How to Communicate without Fuss or Fear Instantly! (Japanese Phrasebook) is a compact phrasebook and introductory guide to the Japanese language, designed specifically for travelers and others seeking to acquire functional communication skills quickly without formal classes.

Authored by Boyé Lafayette De Mente, the book compiles hundreds of essential words and expressions for everyday situations in Japan, presenting them in Romanized form, phonetic spellings, and Japanese script (hiragana, katakana, and kanji) to support immediate use.
Practical sections cover everyday situations and daily communication needs for travelers in Japan, with humorous illustrations demonstrating contextual application.

Boyé Lafayette De Mente, who engaged with Japan since the late 1940s through U.S. intelligence work, study at Jochi University in Tokyo, trade journalism, and authorship of over seventy books on Japanese culture and language, crafted the guide to enable effective interaction with minimal prior knowledge.

Boyé Lafayette De Mente (November 12, 1928 – May 12, 2017) was an American author, journalist, and expert on Japanese and East Asian cultures who produced numerous practical guides to language and communication in the region.

He first arrived in Japan in the late 1940s as a decoding technician with the U.S. Army Security Agency during the Allied Occupation, where he edited a unit newspaper and began his long engagement with the country.
De Mente remained deeply involved with Japan for decades through roles as a student, trade journalist, magazine editor, and prolific author based in Tokyo.

He earned a degree in Japanese and economics from Jochi University (now Sophia University) in Tokyo by attending classes at night while working, and he also graduated from The American Institute for Foreign Trade (now Thunderbird School of Global Management).

These educational credentials, combined with his extended immersion in Japan since the late 1940s and subsequent experiences in Korea and China, equipped him with firsthand expertise in Asian languages and intercultural communication.

De Mente authored over 70 books focused on Japanese language, culture, business practices, and etiquette, many of which served as accessible resources for Western readers seeking to navigate practical interactions in Japan.

stands out through its subtitle "How to Communicate without Fuss or Fear Instantly!," reinforcing the series-wide focus on quick, low-stress mastery of Japanese for everyday interactions.

Survival Japanese: How to Communicate without Fuss or Fear Instantly! (Japanese Phrasebook) is a compact phrasebook and introductory language guide designed to help users achieve functional communication in Japanese quickly and confidently without the need for extensive formal classes.

It targets busy travelers, students, and business professionals who require practical phrases and vocabulary for everyday situations in Japan, emphasizing ease of use and the elimination of fear or hesitation in speaking.

The book's approach allows individuals with limited time to learn essential Japanese on the go, focusing on immediate applicability in real-world settings such as travel, dining, directions, and basic interactions.

Unlike conventional phrasebooks that provide only memorized expressions or dictionaries that offer word-for-word translations, this resource combines essential vocabulary with beginner-level instruction on pronunciation, grammar fundamentals, and language structure to deliver a deeper understanding of Japanese.
The result is a practical tool that enables users to speak Japanese without fuss or fear, tailored for those who need quick, effective results in diverse contexts.
The book is organized into two primary sections: Common Japanese Expressions and Key Words, and Japanese Pronunciation Guides for Key Japanese Names and Signs.

Additional components include a concise history and background of the Japanese language, a pronunciation guide, a basic grammar overview covering elements such as word order, question formation, singular versus plural forms, and formal versus informal speech, and a short dictionary.

Throughout the book, Japanese words and phrases are presented in Romanized form, accompanied by phonetic spellings for pronunciation and authentic Japanese script (including Kanji and Kana) to facilitate both learning and practical use when showing the text to native speakers.

Survival Japanese employs a distinctive triple presentation format for every word and phrase, displaying each entry in Romanized (romaji) form, phonetic spelling to guide pronunciation (for example, "hoteru" for hotel rendered as "hoe-tay-rue"), and authentic Japanese script incorporating Kanji and Kana.
This approach enables users to attempt spoken communication while providing a reliable fallback, as the Japanese script can be shown directly to native speakers when pronunciation difficulties arise.

In the past, if you wanted to translate a text written in Japanese into a foreign language, you had to use translation software, look things up in a dictionary, or in some cases, hire a professional. Especially with long articles or technical content, simply replacing words did not convey the meaning correctly, and it required a significant amount of time and effort.

However, today, thanks to advancements in AI translation and automatic translation technology, articles written in Japanese are being converted into various languages, such as English and Korean, in a short amount of time.

This is not just a story about translation becoming more convenient. It is a major change where the reach of information shared by individuals has changed significantly, and articles that were previously limited to those who could understand Japanese now have the potential to reach overseas readers.
1. The major change of articles written in Japanese turning into foreign languages
Until now, when an individual wrote an article on the internet, the people who could understand that information were basically limited to those who could read Japanese.
As a result, even if the text was written in Japanese, people overseas can now understand the content in a form close to their native language.

Things that are taken for granted in Japan may feel fresh to people overseas.
Conversely, by reading the article, overseas readers may gain new perspectives on ways of thinking and cultural differences that are not well known in Japan.

Japanese has expressions that omit the subject and phrasing that changes meaning depending on the relationship with the other party. Such text can sometimes have a different meaning than originally intended during translation.
However, now, a method where you write your thoughts in Japanese and AI or automatic translation technology converts them into another language has become realistic.
Just by writing your experiences, thoughts, and what you feel daily in Japanese, there is a possibility that someone somewhere in the world will understand the content.
Also, considering the possibility that overseas readers will read it, it is also effective to add simple explanations about systems, culture, and events unique to Japan.
